chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayoub, from 'Umar ibn Aban who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the 'weak ones' (al-mustad'afin), so he said: 'They are the people of Wilayah.' I said, 'Which Wilayah?' He said: 'Indeed, it is not the Wilayah in the Religion, but it is the Wilayah regarding marriage, inheritance, and social mingling. And they are not among the believers, nor among the disbelievers, and among them are those hoped for regarding the Command of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.'

key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weak ones (a specific group in Shia fiqh)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of al-mustad'afin and their specific type of Wilayah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes the 'Mustad'afin' as a distinct intermediate category (neither Mu'min nor Kafir) whose Wilayah is primarily civil and social, governing marriage, inheritance, and daily interaction. This distinction allows for their inclusion in the broader community of believers for practical legal purposes while acknowledging their potential for doctrinal ambiguity or hope in divine decree.
